hook: In Iceland, sidewalks are kept free of ice by hot water piped from underground, and most homes are heated the same way. In Minnesota, a school stays warm in January using pipes buried in its playing field. Both tap the same source, Earth's internal heat, in very different ways.

prereq.q: What causes plate tectonics and volcanoes?
options: Heat from Earth's interior driving convection in the mantle
prereq.why: Interior heat drives mantle convection, which moves plates and feeds volcanoes.

prereq.q: In a power plant, what turns the generator?
options: A turbine spun by steam or another moving fluid
prereq.why: A turbine spun by steam turns the generator.

options: Unstable nuclei giving off radiation and changing into other elements
prereq.why: Decay of radioactive elements also heats Earth's interior.

figure.caption: Left: a geothermal power plant uses steam from hot rock near a plate boundary. Right: a ground source heat pump moves heat between a house and shallow ground.

chain.cause: Radioactive decay and leftover heat warm Earth's interior
chain.effect: heat flows outward and is close to the surface near plate boundaries and volcanoes

chain.cause: Wells bring up underground steam and hot water
chain.effect: the steam spins a turbine and generator, day and night, with no fuel burned

chain.cause: Cooled water is pumped back down
chain.effect: the reservoir is refilled so the heat source is not depleted

chain.cause: A few meters down, the ground stays about the same temperature all year
chain.effect: a ground source heat pump can heat a building in winter and cool it in summer almost anywhere

ideas: Geothermal energy is heat from Earth's interior, from radioactive decay and heat left from Earth's formation. It is renewable when managed.
Power plants need very hot water or steam near the surface, found near plate boundaries and hot spots (Iceland, New Zealand, California). They run day and night.
A ground source heat pump uses electricity to move heat between a building and shallow ground, which stays at a steady temperature, so it works almost anywhere.
Drawbacks: few suitable sites for power plants, high drilling costs, release of hydrogen sulfide and dissolved minerals, and depletion if water is withdrawn faster than it is replaced.

misconception.wrong: Geothermal energy is the sun's heat stored in the ground, so it stops working on cloudy winter days.
misconception.right: Geothermal power comes from Earth's interior heat, so it runs day and night in any weather. Heat pumps use shallow ground, which stays at a steady temperature year-round.

summary: Geothermal energy is heat from Earth's interior. Where hot rock is near the surface, at plate boundaries and hot spots, wells bring up steam to spin turbines day and night, and cooled water is reinjected so the resource lasts. Ground source heat pumps move heat between buildings and the steady-temperature shallow ground almost anywhere. Limits are few good power plant sites, drilling costs, some released gases and the risk of depleting a field.
